# input: 2キロワット かける 3時間
# No number agreement and no space between the number and the unit, on input
# or output. The separators are English's — "," for groups, "." for the
# decimal — and 1, 5 and 1.5 take one and the same word.
# The katakana loans read and the SI symbol prints. ジュール is an alias and
# not a `forms` row, so the joule family comes back as J/kJ/MJ however it went
# キロワット時 fuses the loan with 時 into one token, so the watt-hour is a
# readable word here where English, Russian and Arabic have only a compound.
# It is an alias and not a `forms` row, so it still prints the symbol.
# The myriad. Japanese counts in ten-thousands, so 万 is a magnitude word in
# its own right and 一万 is one of them, not ten of a thousand.
# The word operators need whitespace around them even though Japanese is
# written without any. The symbol operators above have no such requirement.
# A conversion is marked by a case particle glued to the unit rather than by a
# preposition before the target: を and から both do it.
